ops.body: - [owner] **After dark** (after-dark audit 13): with no position, a town up to 150 minutes of solar time from the phone's offset is judged on the phone's clock (Chicago on an Eastern phone: an hour off); with a position, a phone whose clock is set to another zone than where it is draws marks on that clock. A time zone by position would settle both; until then 45 minutes from you, 150 from the offset.

- [owner] **After dark** (after-dark audit 14, steward S2): with the panel closed the map shows the amber lines and the rings with no words; "Only what is mapped" and the reading's time are said only in the panel (the panel holds the words, Nov 5). A quiet line at the map's edge while the layer is on would carry them.

- [owner] **After dark** (after-dark audit 15, steward S6): the lit line's amber (#a87400, chosen for 3:1 on the ground) sits about 20° of hue from the accent; a lighter yellow with a dark casing would keep the contrast without the gold.

- **After dark** (decision 0181): three calls deferred from the audit, in `docs/DEFERRED.md` under After dark: the "near you" rule for hours (audit 13), words on the map while the panel is closed (audit 14), and the amber's nearness to the accent (audit 15). Also: VISION.md is at its byte budget, so 0181 has no Precedents row yet; and the panel's ground and the heads-up's width were rejected as older shared components.

argv: on a phone set to another time zone
after-dark audit 13: with a position, the rule compares the map to where you are
ops.body: - [ ] **Do:** on a phone in Allentown after sunset, turn on After dark on Explore and browse to a town 2,000 km west. **Expect:** near you the rings show; over the far town no rings, and the line under the switch says "Hours read only near you" (DK4, after-dark audit 13)
